What can policy actually change?

Mechanisms, not promises.
01 / SUPPLY

What can be built

Zoning rules set where and what housing may be built. A rule change allows development; it doesn’t guarantee homes are built or rents fall.

Read HUD’s discussion ↗
02 / HOUSEHOLD SUPPORT

What you pay directly

Rental assistance can reduce eligible households’ payments. Eligibility, funding, local availability, and waiting lists matter.

Explore housing vouchers ↗
03 / FINANCING

The cost of borrowing

A different mortgage rate changes a buyer’s payment. Use the buying scenario to isolate that effect while holding the home price fixed.

Understand a loan estimate ↗
What we can’t tell you yet

This prototype does not establish why rent is high in your neighborhood. It has no local price data, current bill tracker, or causal policy model. Timing, development costs, demand, and implementation can change outcomes.

CHECK OUR WORK

Every explanation needs a foundation.

01 · REFERENCE STANDARD

Housing cost burden ↗

California HCD · Housing costs, including utilities, above 30% of gross income are generally considered cost burdened. A screening reference, not an individual budget.

02 · MODEL FOUNDATION

Beyond the mortgage payment ↗

Consumer Financial Protection Bureau · Principal and interest are only part of the payment. Taxes, insurance, and mortgage insurance may also apply.

Reference pages checked October 25, 2026. All dollar amounts and rates start as invented examples, not market observations. No active legislation is represented.

HOUSING LAB · MVP 0.1
ABOUT CIVICLENS

Clarity before conclusions.

This prototype connects plain-language questions to a small, curated housing explainer and deterministic calculators. Question routing is keyword based; no LLM runs in this version.

Reference facts, hypothetical arithmetic, and uncertain policy outcomes are kept separate. No analytics, account, browser storage, or financial-input API calls are used.

Future AI should retrieve verified evidence and explain validated model outputs, with citations and explicit limits. It should never invent a bill, a forecast, or a calculation.
